subproblem.title: Closure theorem in degree d + 1 < P from BR_P(d) and CL*_{P,d+1} by localization (parent V1–V2, Simon 6.8.3(1))
subproblem.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC), (VO) (types of the accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, dtc_vanish_off_support). Let P, d ∈ ℕ with d + 1 < P and assume BR_P(d) (as in sibling boundary_im) and CL*_{P,d+1} (as in sibling closure_compact). Then CL_P(d+1): for every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), if every T_j is IM, sup_j(M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U and T_j ⇀ T, then T is IM.

B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P d : ℕ), d + 1 < P → (∀ (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity R → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → R.boundary.massOn W < ∞) → IsIntegerMultiplicity R.boundary) → (∀ (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (d + 1)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j).boundary) → (∀ j, (Ts j).support ⊆ K) → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).mass + (Ts j).boundary.mass) < ∞ → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) → (∀ (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (d + 1)), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent V1–V2 (Simon 6.8.3(1)). Uses (SL) and (REP), (T1), (T2), (MM), (IML) of sibling foundations.
1. ∂T_j is IM by BR_P(d) in U; T and ∂T have locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity) and (REP) represents them.
2. Fix x₀ ∈ U with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U and G := B_{r₀}(x₀). The IMRep measures μ_j, μ'_j of T_j, ∂T_j give admissible representations ((IMC)(d)) with locally bounded masses ((MR)); (T1) gives a subsequence and μ with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).
3. (SL) with f := |· − x₀| and (MM) give r ∈ (0, r₀) with liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞ and μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0; pass to a subsequence with sup_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞; a cut-off near the sphere gives M(Z_{j,r}) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}).
4. T'_j := T_j⌞B_r(x₀) is IM ((IMC)(b)), spt T'_j ⊆ B̄_r(x₀), sup_j(M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j)) < ∞, and (T2) gives T'_j ⇀ A_r := T⌞B_r(x₀).
5. For ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U; [0, 1]) with ζ = 1 near B̄_r(x₀), T̂'_j(ω) := T'_j(ζω) are IM currents in ℝ^P (same IMReps) with spt ⊆ B̄_r(x₀), bounded masses and boundary masses (∂T̂'_j(η) = ∂T'_j(ζη) by (VO)), T̂'_j ⇀ Â_r(ω) := A_r(ζω), and ∂T̂'_j is IM by BR_P(d) in ℝ^P.
6. CL*_{P,d+1} shows that Â_r is IM. On B_r(x₀), Â_r = A_r = T, so T|_{B_r(x₀)} is IM by (IML)(2); since x₀ is arbitrary, (IML)(1) shows that T is IM. ∎
Note: accepted cbrcs_localize_at_point covers steps 2–4 and cbrcs_ce_* cover parts of step 5.
proof_key_steps: Good radius and IM restrictions with bounded masses.

audit.reason: Good-radius restriction and extension produce the common compact support and uniform mass bounds required by CL*. Boundary integrality follows from the assumed BR_P(d), and locality recovers closure on U. Together with the other children, this closes the checked induction and yields the selected parent statement.
